SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.220833, -71.767500 (Explicit)
Reported Spill Volume: 5 gallons
Report Description
UP TO 5 GALLONS OF WASTEWATER CONTAINING INCINERATOR ASH RELEASED FROM A VENT TO AN ABOVE GROUND STORAGE TANK CALLED THE "DUMP TANK". THE RELEASE IMPACTED PAVED SURFACES. NO STORM DRAINS, SOIL OR GROUNDWATER WAS IMPACTED. THE TANK IS USED TO STORE CONTACT WATER AND OTHER WASTE WATER CONTAINING ASH PRIOR TO PUMPING THE MATERIAL TO A FILTER PRESS FOR TREATMENT. FACILITY PERSONNEL HAD AIR-PRESSURIZED A LINE TO THE TANK TO REMOVE A BLOCKAGE. THE PRESSURIZATION CAUSED WASTEWATER AND SOLIDS TO OVERFLOW FROM THE TANK'S VENT. THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR THIS MATERIAL TO BE A RCRA CHARACTERISTIC WASTE AND AS SUCH, THIS RELEASE IS BEING REPORTED AS A PRECAUTION. SUBSEQUENT TESTING OF THE MATERIAL MAY DETERMINE OTHERWISE.

Report DescriptionINITIAL/FINAL INCIDENT TYPE: SEARCH AND RESCUE LOCATION: POINT COUVERDEN, AK TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 0909Z TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 2055Z NAME OF REPORTING UNIT: USCG SECTOR SOUTHEAST ALASKA AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • AT 0909Z, USCG SECTOR SOUTHEAST ALASKA RECEIVED A MAYDAY CALL ON VHF FROM F/V WIND WALKER REPORTING THE VESSEL WAS OVERTURNING AND THEY WERE EVACUATING INTO A LIFE RAFT. • D17 CORRELATED AN EPIRB ALERT THAT WAS RECEIVED AT THE SAME TIME REGISTERED TO THE VESSEL. • IT IS BELIEVED THAT THERE WERE 5 PERSONS ON THE VESSEL, AS NOAA BOARDING OFFICERS PERFORMED A BOARDING ON THE VESSEL YESTERDAY. • SECTOR SOUTHEAST ALASKA LAUNCHED A HELICOPTER FROM AIR STATION SITKA AND A SMALL BOAT FROM STATION JUNEAU. • SECTOR SOUTHEAST ALASKA REDIRECTED CGC HEALY AND CGC DOUGLAS DENMAN TO THE SCENE. • THE USCG SEARCH ASSETS COULD NOT DETECT THE VESSEL OR ANY DEBRIS IN THE SEARCH AREA DUE TO WEATHER CONDITIONS. • ON-SCENE WEATHER ARE WINDS AT 34KTS AND SEAS 5-10 FT WITH LOW VISIBILITY, ICE, AND SNOW. • A SELF LOCATING DATA MARKING BUOY AND 04 SURVIVAL SUITS WERE LOCATED IN THE SEARCH AREA, AND 03 SURVIVAL SUITS LOCATED ASHORE. • CGC HEALY AND CGC DOUGLAS DENMAN WERE DIVERTED AND REMAIN SEARCHING ON-SCENE. • AN ALASKA MARINE HIGHWAY FERRY SEARCHED FOR 08 HOURS WITH NOTHING FOUND. • STATION JUNEAU WILL RETURN TO BASE DUE TO SIGNIFICANT CREW FATIGUE AND TRANSIT TIME. • THE HELICOPTER FROM AIR STATION SITKA WILL BE DEPARTING WITHIN 30 MINUTES DUE TO FUEL CONSTRAINTS. • THERE IS LOCAL MEDIA INTEREST IN THIS INCIDENT. • THE CURRENT SEARCH PLAN IS TO KEEP CGC HEALY AND CGC DOUGLAS DENMAN ON-SCENE TO CONDUCT SEARCH PATTERNS. • AT THIS TIME, THE INDIVIDUALS WOULD HAVE BEEN IN THE WATER FOR GREATER THAN 12 HOURS. • ON-SCENE WEATHER CONTINUES TO BE STRONG WINDS AND WINTER TEMPERATURES. • THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREA COMMAND CENTERS.

properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 894202
Incident Time: 2009-01-07 17:00:00
Nearest City: Uniontown, PA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: AUTOMOBILE PAINT
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: THE CITY OF UNIONTOWN
Skytruth Analysis
AT LEAST 2 LARGE ROLLOFF LOADS OF TOXIC WASTE WAS DUMPED AT A SITE AT THE UNIONTOWN SEWAGE TREATMENT PLANT. THIS MATERIAL WAS FROM AN AUTOMOBILE PARTS STORE LOCATED AT 80 EAST FAYETTE ST IN UNIONTOWN THAT WENT OUT OF BUSINESS. THIS MATERIAL INCLUDED AUTOMOBILE PAINT AND THINNERS, OIL, GREASE, AND EVERYTHING ELSE ONE WOULD FIND IN A PARTS STORE. CITY TRUCKS, ONE DRIVEN BY THE CITIES MAYOR HAULED THIS MATERIAL TO THE TREATMENT PLANT AND DUMPED IT IN THE VERY EARLY HOURS APPROXIMATELY MID SEPTEMBER. THE CITY HAS ALSO BEEN DUMPING REFUSE FROM DEMOLISHED HOUSES IN THE SAME AREA. THESE HOUSES WERE RECENTLY ACQUIRED BY THE CITY FOR A NEW DEVELOPMENT AND WERE PROBABLY NOT CLEARED OF ASBESTOS AND OTHER HAZARDS, THEY WERE DEMOLISHED BY CITY EMPLOYEES. THIS DUMP SITE WAS COVERED WITH BACKFILL, ALSO BEFORE DAYLITE IN THE MORNING. MULCH WAS USED TO COVER THE ODOR OF THE PAINT AND THINNERS.
